changes.text: 本篇的全部过程都出自沙克尔顿本人的叙述（这里用的是1920年印本的 OCR 文本），是当事人、领导者的记述。没有取得其他队员的日记作对照。他的叙述写到了队员的状态：大家筋疲力尽；第二次尝试受挫、被迫后撤时，全队大失所望；部分人一度消沉，随即恢复。这些也都出自他的叙述。但营地里其他人是否同意海洋营的决定，证据里没有，本篇也不另替他们猜测心理。文中那句“喝过更干净的水”出自一位未具名队员的日记，是经沙克尔顿转引的。

Everything in this piece comes from Shackleton's own narrative, read here through the OCR text of the 1920 printing: the account of a participant who led the party. No other member's diary has been brought in for comparison. His narrative does report the men's state: they were all exhausted; at the second setback, when they had to retreat, there was intense disappointment among all of them; and an apathy that took hold of some of the men soon passed. These reports, too, come from his narrative. Whether anyone else in the camp agreed with the Ocean Camp decision is not in the evidence, and this piece does not put further feelings in their mouths. The line about the sip of water comes from an unnamed member's diary, as quoted by Shackleton.

一种解释是（作者推断），海洋营不是他第一次决定停下。行军第二天早上，雪大得看不清路，他就决定不拔营；天晴一些后探到一块好走的浮冰，午饭后又继续走。两次决定都在衡量眼前的路还能不能走下去。扎营等待也不是新想法：在第一个营地，冰面一夜裂开两次；那一夜之后，他已经写下过在最近的厚浮冰上扎营、等浮冰外漂到开阔水面的方案。但他确信应当先尝试行军，还特别提到这个问题有心理层面的考虑：让大家觉得自己正在朝陆地走，比坐等漂流要好。海洋营是在四天苦干之后回到这个先前暂且搁置、留作退路的方案。营地选在更结实的浮冰上，理由里挂着一个具体的指望：附近可能开出水道，那时可以划船去找陆地。等条件更有利，再做第二次尝试。

One reading, and it is the author's, is that Ocean Camp was not the first time he chose to stop. On the march's second morning, with snow too thick to see a path, he decided not to strike camp; when it cleared and a good floe turned up, they moved on after lunch. Both decisions turned on whether the way ahead could be made. Nor was camping to wait a new idea. At their first camp the ice split twice in one night. After that night he had already written down the option of camping on the nearest heavy floe and awaiting the outward drift of the pack to open water. But he felt sure it was right to attempt a march first, noting that there was a psychological aspect too: the men would be better off feeling they were on their way to land than simply sitting and waiting for the drift. Ocean Camp, after four days of hard effort, was a return to that option he had set aside. The camp went onto a more solid floe, and the reasoning carried a specific hope: leads opening nearby, boats in the water, land to the north-west. A second attempt was to follow once conditions improved.
后来他们真的做了第二次尝试。途中一度因前方冰面无法通行，只好后撤半英里，换到更结实的浮冰上扎营，全队大失所望。行军七天，直线只前进了七英里半；照这个速度，要三百多天才能到西边的陆地，而食物只够四十二天，只好再次在浮冰上扎营。新的营地叫耐心营，他们在那里住了将近三个半月。

Later they did make that second attempt. At one point the ice ahead proved impassable, and, to the intense disappointment of all, they had to retreat half a mile to get onto a stronger floe and camp. They marched for seven days and gained seven and a half miles in a direct line; at that rate it would take over three hundred days to reach the land to the west, and they had food for only forty-two days. So they camped once more on the floe. They called the new camp Patience Camp and lived there for nearly three and a half months.

dispositions.rationale: limits.0 原称别人怎么想不在证据里，与证据矛盾。现改为：他的叙述记有队员筋疲力尽、第二次受挫时全队失望、部分人一度消沉随即恢复；证据里确实没有的，只是其他人是否同意海洋营的决定。中英文已同步，并在 ev 中补入相应证据。

evidence.quote: to the intense disappointment of all
THE apathy which seemed to take possession of some of the men at the frustration of their hopes was soon dispelled.

dispositions.rationale: 中文“先前否决过的方案”改为“先前暂且搁置、留作退路的方案”。证据表明，在厚浮冰上扎营等待是附条件的备选，他只是决定先尝试行军，并未否决这个方案。改后与英文“set aside”一致，英文不变。

evidence.quote: We could even, if progress proved too difficult and too injurious to the boats
We will make an attempt to move.

dispositions.rationale: 已按补入的 S-E24、S-E25 核对。limits.0 关于队员情绪的错误说法已随 F1 一并修正。story.13 补入第二次尝试受挫的经过：前方冰面无法通行，被迫后撤半英里，全队大失所望；ev 加入 S-E24。其余结局叙述与 S-E21、S-E8 一致。

evidence.quote: the ice ahead proved quite unnegotiable
we had to retire half a mile so as to get on a stronger floe
As we only had food for forty-two days there was no alternative
